name: Zurich
description: The most populous canton and Switzerland's economic engine: a global financial centre, the ETH federal institute of technology, the country's main airport and a lively lakeside city regularly ranked among the most liveable in the world.

name: Bern
description: Seat of the federal government and the second-largest canton, bilingual and stretching from the Jura hills to the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau. The medieval old town of Bern, with its arcades and fountains, is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

name: Lucerne
description: Gateway to central Switzerland on Lake Lucerne, with the wooden Chapel Bridge, the Lion Monument and the KKL concert hall. Mount Pilatus and the Rigi, reached by the world's first mountain cogwheel railway, rise just above the city.

name: Uri
description: One of the three founding cantons of 1291 and the land of William Tell, whose legend is set in Altdorf. The Gotthard pass and the Gotthard Base Tunnel, the longest railway tunnel in the world, make Uri the key passage between north and south.

name: Schwyz
description: The canton that gave Switzerland its name and its red flag with a white cross. The Federal Charter of 1291 is kept in the town of Schwyz, Einsiedeln Abbey is a major pilgrimage site, and Victorinox makes the Swiss Army knife in Ibach.

name: Obwalden
description: A small half-canton of lakes and pastures around Sarnen, home of Niklaus von Flüe, the hermit and patron saint of Switzerland. The resort of Engelberg, an enclave of the canton, leads to the glaciers of the Titlis.

name: Nidwalden
description: A half-canton squeezed between Lake Lucerne and the mountains, with Stans at its centre. The Stanserhorn, the Bürgenstock resort and the Pilatus aircraft factory are its best-known landmarks.

name: Glarus
description: A single narrow Alpine valley that still votes its laws by a show of hands at the open-air Landsgemeinde. An early industrial canton, it passed Switzerland's first factory law in 1864, and its Sardona thrust is a UNESCO geological site.

name: Zug
description: Small, wealthy and famous for its low taxes, Zug hosts the headquarters of commodity traders and the blockchain companies of the "Crypto Valley". The old town lies on the lake, and the local cherries flavour the Zuger Kirschtorte.

name: Fribourg
description: A bilingual canton on the language border, with a medieval city on a bend of the Sarine river and a bilingual university. Gruyère cheese, the castle of Gruyères and the double cream of the Pre-Alps are its culinary emblems.

name: Solothurn
description: Its capital is considered the most beautiful baroque town in Switzerland, with a curious devotion to the number eleven: eleven churches, eleven fountains and a clock with eleven hours. The canton stretches from the Jura ridges to the Aare plain.

name: Basel-Stadt
description: The smallest canton by area, essentially the city of Basel on the Rhine, at the point where Switzerland, France and Germany meet. A world hub of the pharmaceutical industry, home of Art Basel and of the country's oldest university, founded in 1460.

name: Basel-Landschaft
description: The rural half of Basel, separated from the city in 1833 after a short civil war. It holds the Roman city of Augusta Raurica, the best-preserved Roman site north of the Alps, and a strong chemical and life-science industry.

name: Schaffhausen
description: The northernmost canton, lying almost entirely on the German side of the Rhine. The Rhine Falls, the largest waterfall in Europe by volume, and the circular Munot fortress above the old town are its landmarks.

name: Appenzell Ausserrhoden
description: The Protestant half of Appenzell, a land of rolling green hills and gabled wooden houses around Herisau. Once a centre of the textile and embroidery trade, it keeps strong traditions of yodelling and alpine cattle drives.

name: Appenzell Innerrhoden
description: The least populous canton, Catholic and deeply traditional, still decides its laws by a show of hands at the Landsgemeinde on the square of Appenzell. Appenzeller cheese and the Alpstein massif with the Säntis are its pride.

name: St. Gallen
description: Built around the abbey of St. Gallen, whose baroque library is a UNESCO World Heritage site. The canton reaches from Lake Constance to the Alps and was for centuries the world capital of embroidery; today it hosts a leading business university.

name: Graubünden
description: The largest canton and the only trilingual one, with 150 valleys and the Romansh language. It hosts the resorts of St. Moritz and Davos, the Swiss National Park and the Rhaetian Railway, a UNESCO site, while Chur is the oldest town in Switzerland.

name: Aargau
description: Named after the Aare river, the "water canton" where the Aare, Reuss and Limmat join the Rhine. It is the cradle of the Habsburg dynasty, whose ancestral castle still stands, and the heart of Switzerland's energy industry with three nuclear power plants.

name: Thurgau
description: A gentle canton of orchards and vineyards along Lake Constance, nicknamed "Mostindien" for its apple cider. Napoleon III spent his youth at Arenenberg castle, now a museum overlooking the lake.

name: Ticino
description: The only canton entirely Italian-speaking, with a Mediterranean feel, palm trees and the lakes of Lugano and Locarno. The three medieval castles of Bellinzona are a UNESCO site and Locarno hosts a major international film festival.

name: Vaud
description: The largest French-speaking canton, on the shores of Lake Léman. Lausanne is the Olympic capital, the terraced vineyards of Lavaux are a UNESCO site, and the canton hosts the EPFL, the Montreux Jazz Festival and the castle of Chillon.

name: Valais
description: The canton of the Matterhorn and of most Swiss peaks above 4,000 metres, bilingual along the upper Rhône valley. It is the largest wine region of the country, home to Zermatt and Verbier and to the Great Aletsch Glacier, the longest in the Alps.

name: Neuchâtel
description: The cradle of Swiss watchmaking: La Chaux-de-Fonds and Le Locle, planned around the watch industry, are UNESCO World Heritage sites. Vineyards line the lake, and the canton was a Prussian principality until 1848 even after joining the Confederation.

name: Geneva
description: An international city at the tip of Lake Léman, hosting the European headquarters of the United Nations, the Red Cross and CERN, where the web was invented. Private banking, luxury watchmaking and the Jet d'Eau are its other trademarks.

name: Jura
description: The youngest canton, created in 1979 after separating from Bern. A francophone land of forests and pastures where the Franches-Montagnes horse is bred, with watchmaking in Porrentruy and the wild gorges of the Doubs.
